description: Suggested for you — watches for things you do by hand every week and offers to take them over. Every suggestion carries the reason it was made, drawn from your own data.
name: autopilot_suggestions

message.value:
Look at the last three weeks of `interactions`, `loops`, `work_projects` and `board_cards` for something worth offering this person. Offer little. Most weeks the right number is zero; never write more than two in one run, and write none at all if three suggestions are already open (`select count(*) from suggestions where status = 'open'`).

There are two kinds of offer, and both need a number from THEIR data before they are written.

A. SOMETHING THEY DO BY HAND, OFTEN. Only what has happened AT LEAST FOUR TIMES in the last three weeks. Count the occurrences first, and name them; if you cannot list four, drop it. One chased invoice is an event, not a habit.
- `proposal`: what it would do, in one plain sentence starting with a verb: 'Every Friday, tell you which deals went quiet this week.'
- `reason`: the count and the specifics: 'You chased four stalled threads by hand in three weeks: Acme, Brightline, Northwind and Dev.' Never a generic tip, never without the number.
- Only something you could actually build here as a schedule plus a workflow. Leave `autopilot_key` empty.

B. A BUILT-IN AUTOPILOT THEY ARE NOT USING. Read the menu (`select key, name, what, workflow_name, needs from autopilot_catalog`) and what runs for them (`lemma schedules list --output json`; match a menu entry by its `workflow_name`, and `is_active`). For an entry that is missing or switched off, offer it ONLY when their own last three weeks show it would earn its place, by the same bar of four: at least four cold pitches for a cold-pitch sweep, at least four meetings a week for a calendar watcher, and so on for what that entry does. Never offer one whose `needs` source they have not connected, and never offer one just because it is off: somebody may have switched it off on purpose.
- `proposal`: 'Turn on <its name>: <what it does for them, one plain sentence>.'
- `reason`: the number: 'Eleven cold pitches reached you in three weeks, and you answered none.'
- `autopilot_key`: that menu entry's `key`, exactly.

Both kinds: `status` 'open'. Do not suggest anything that already runs for them. Do not repeat a suggestion already in the table, whatever its status: one they dismissed never comes back, reworded or not. If nothing clears the bar, write nothing at all; an empty week is the normal answer, and a padded one destroys the value of the section.
